:::caution[Superseded: runtime-DDL ensures are removed]
This runbook documents the lazy-`CREATE TABLE`-at-runtime pattern that has
since been **removed** (plan `self-contained-migration-baseline-2026-06-02`).
Schema is now **migrations-only**: one squashed
`libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/000-baseline.sql` + idempotent incrementals
(`107+`). The `ensure-schema.ts` / `ensure-schema-dogfood.ts` files no longer
exist, and there is no `ensureMyTable` / `ensureAllDogfoodTables` family — to
change the schema, **add a migration**, never an `ensureXxx()` / inline
`CREATE TABLE` in runtime code (see `/internal/docs/system/storage-policy`).
The only surviving piece is the `globalThis`-pinned-flag idea, which now lives
in `packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/boot-gate.ts` purely as a
projection **boot-readiness gate** (`globalThis.__papercuspEnsureFlags` with
`sql_migrations_complete` / `runtime_ensure_complete`) — not for table
creation. The prose below is preserved for the historical pattern + the
still-true PG idempotency facts (`CREATE … IF NOT EXISTS`, `ADD COLUMN IF NOT
EXISTS`, the flag-after-await discipline).
:::

## What

The operator creates several `harness_shared` tables at runtime
(not via migrations) — `ensure-schema.ts` for the original surface,
`ensure-schema-dogfood.ts` for v5's new dogfood tables. Both use the
same pattern:

```ts
type Flags = {
  myTable: boolean;
  /* ... */
};

type _G = { __myEnsureFlags?: Flags };
const _g = globalThis as unknown as _G;
const flags: Flags =
  _g.__myEnsureFlags ?? (_g.__myEnsureFlags = { myTable: false, /* ... */ });

export async function ensureMyTable(): Promise<void> {
  if (flags.myTable) return;
  const { sql } = getOrgPg();
  await sql.unsafe(`
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS harness_shared.my_table (
      workspace_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
      id BIGSERIAL,
      /* ... */
      PRIMARY KEY (workspace_id, id)
    );
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS my_table_thing_idx
      ON harness_shared.my_table (workspace_id, thing);
  `);
  flags.myTable = true;
}
```

Three load-bearing properties:

1. **`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`** + **`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`**
   — both are PG-side idempotent. Re-running the statement is a no-op.
2. **The flag is set AFTER the await**, not inside the SQL. If the
   `sql.unsafe(...)` call throws (PG down, partial failure,
   permission error, …), `flags.myTable` stays `false` and the next
   call will retry the full statement. PG's idempotency handles the
   "already done" parts.
3. **The flag is pinned to `globalThis`** so Turbopack HMR / dev-mode
   module reloads don't reset it. Without the pin, every dev-mode
   code edit re-runs the full DDL on next call — slow + visible in
   PG logs.

## Why the `globalThis` pin matters

Turbopack reloads modules on edit. A top-level `const flags = {...}`
gets re-initialized to `{ myTable: false, ... }` every reload. The
next caller sees the false flag, re-runs the DDL. Harmless (PG
shrugs), but:

- Slow if you have 12+ ensure-fns — each call pays the round-trip
  cost.
- Visible in PG logs as repeated DDL statements.
- Confusing during diagnosis: "why is my ensure being called every
  request?"

The `globalThis` pin parks the flag table at a process-level
singleton that survives module reloads.

```ts
// ensure-schema-dogfood.ts uses key __dogfoodEnsureFlags
type _G = { __dogfoodEnsureFlags?: DogfoodFlags };
```

Each ensure family picks its own symbol so the namespaces don't
collide (`__dogfoodEnsureFlags`, `__syncNotifyDedupe`, etc.).

## Calling pattern: batch helper

The companion to per-fn ensures is a batch helper:

```ts
export async function ensureAllDogfoodTables(): Promise<void> {
  await Promise.all([
    ensureFeatureQueueTable(),
    ensureContributorsTable(),
    /* ... */
  ]);
}
```

`Promise.all` is fine because each ensure has its own
flag-guard + the underlying CREATE statements are independent.
After first successful call, subsequent calls short-circuit at
the if-flag check; the only network round-trip is the first one
per process.

When to call the batch helper:
- At process boot in `instrumentation-node.ts` (fire-and-forget).
- Before the projection process starts reading (gate: tables exist).
- In tests that need the schema (the live verifier scripts do this).

## "I added a column to an existing table" pitfall

The pattern handles "table missing" gracefully but NOT "table is
out of date." If you change the DDL string in `ensureMyTable`:

- Old PG already has the table from a prior boot.
- `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` sees the table exists and skips.
- The new column never lands.

Fix: use `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` in the same
`sql.unsafe(...)` block after the CREATE:

```ts
await sql.unsafe(`
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS harness_shared.my_table (...);
  ALTER TABLE harness_shared.my_table
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS new_col TEXT;
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS my_table_new_col_idx
    ON harness_shared.my_table (new_col);
`);
```

`ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` is idempotent (PG 9.6+). The PR diff
adds the new ALTER inline; bumping a version in your flag isn't
needed.

## Graceful-skip for missing pre-existing tables (P-019 part 2 case)

When you're attaching triggers to tables you didn't create — e.g.,
`harness_features_consolidated` from `001-shared.sql` — those
tables may not exist yet on a freshly-installed harness before
`scaffold-harness` has run. The pattern:

```ts
for (const tableName of EXISTING_HYPERBEE_REACTIVE_TABLES) {
  try {
    await sql.unsafe(
      'CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER emit_change_notify_trg ' +
        'AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ' +
        'ON harness_shared.' + tableName + ' ' +
        'FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION harness_shared.emit_change_notify()',
    );
  } catch (e: unknown) {
    const msg = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);
    if (/does not exist|relation .* does not exist/i.test(msg)) {
      // Table not yet provisioned in this workspace — fine, will retry
      // on next boot. Don't log noisily.
      continue;
    }
    throw e;
  }
}
```

The try/catch on the `does not exist` substring is the right
shape: don't promote it to a fatal error because the table will
appear later when scaffold runs. Re-throw any other error.

## What NOT to do

- **Don't set the flag inside the await call.** `flags.x = true; await sql.unsafe(...)` would mark success before PG confirmed; an error would wedge the in-process flag.
- **Don't bypass the flag with "the ensure is cheap."** Even
  cheap calls add up: 100 page loads × 12 ensures = 1200 PG
  round-trips per session if the flag isn't doing its job.
- **Don't use `CREATE TABLE` (without IF NOT EXISTS)** — first
  retry will error.
- **Don't put DDL inside a transaction that also does DML.** Mixed
  DDL+DML transactions have surprising lock-promotion semantics.
  Ensures are DDL-only; let app code use its own transaction for
  the row writes that follow.
- **Don't pull the DDL into a `.sql` migration file when it's a
  runtime ensure.** Once a table is in `ensure-schema*.ts`, leave
  it there — moving it to a numbered SQL file creates a migration-
  ordering question (does my new boot run the new SQL file or
  the old ensure-fn first?). Pick one location.
